title: Comparative Education

items.q: The statement “the use of marks gathered during the course, not only a final paper, to decide a grade” describes which of the following?

Elective subject
Vocational subject
Core subject

items.q: Which of the following best describes Junior secondary?

the bending of comparative findings to serve the interest of a government

o: the checking that figures from two countries mean the same thing before they are set side by side
the reading of a system through the beliefs about the person and society held by its founders
the deep study of a single system treated as one whole
the tracing of a system back through time in order to explain its present form
items.s: Philosophical approach: the reading of a system through the beliefs about the person and society held by its founders. The other options describe Historical approach, Case study approach, Equivalence of data.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the movement of an idea for schooling from the country that tried it to another that adopts it”
o: Purpose of comparison
Policy transfer
Educational borrowing
Reform
items.s: Policy transfer is the movement of an idea for schooling from the country that tried it to another that adopts it.

items.q: The correct meaning of UNESCO is
o: the United Nations agency that promotes education, science and culture among member states
the amount spent to keep one pupil in school for one academic year
the United Nations agency that works for the welfare and schooling of children
the transfer of decisions about a school to its own head, staff and committee
items.s: UNESCO: the United Nations agency that promotes education, science and culture among member states. The other options describe Unit cost, School based management, UNICEF.

items.q: In this course, Federal system of education refers to
o: the concentration of decisions about schools in a single national ministry
the Nigerian pattern of six primary years, three junior and three senior secondary years, then four at university
an arrangement in which the national government and the component states share responsibility for schools
a school founded by a religious body and allowed to keep its own ethos
items.s: Federal system of education: an arrangement in which the national government and the component states share responsibility for schools. The other options describe Faith school, Central control, Six-three-three-four.

items.q: In this course, Benchmarking refers to
o: the setting of targets and allocation of resources for a school system over a period of years
the selection of a specific foreign practice that answers a problem at home
the adoption of a practice observed in another country into one's own system
the measuring of one's own provision against the best practice found elsewhere
items.s: Benchmarking: the measuring of one's own provision against the best practice found elsewhere. The other options describe Educational borrowing, Educational planning, Lesson drawing.

items.q: In this course, Area study refers to
o: the close examination of the school system of one country in its own setting
the field that studies school systems in two or more countries in order to understand and improve them
the careful placing of two school systems side by side on the same points of interest
an inquiry that gathers the same data from several countries and analyses it together
items.s: Area study: the close examination of the school system of one country in its own setting. The other options describe Comparative study, Cross-national study, Comparative education.
